Navarra and Aragón

Photo: Miguel Ángel García., CC BY 2.0

Six places to learn. Open one to read its page.

6places to learn
DO
NavarraNavarra

Limestone soils and a Mediterranean climate with a cold, drying wind give wines of medium-high acidity, freshness and a mineral touch.

DO
SomontanoAragón

A strong swing between warm and cool temperatures in August and September, plus distinctive soils, gives fruity, aromatic wines with high acidity.

DO
Campo de BorjaAragón

Scant rain and the dry cierzo wind keep vines under constant water stress, so ripening is slow and wines gain aroma and deep colour.

DO
CariñenaAragón

Varied soils, little rain, extreme temperatures and the cierzo wind make a harsh setting that has kept only hardy vineyards going.

DO
CalatayudAragón

Altitude, big day-night temperature swings and a wide range of soils slow ripening, giving structured wines with colour and a mineral edge.

DO
UrbezoAragón

Deep, stony, well-drained soils and a dry climate with the cierzo wind suit vines on flat ground at about 460 to 495 m.
